commodious

/kuh-MOH-dee-uhs/ - rhymes with melodious · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Commodious means roomy, with comfortable space to spare.

The old station wagon proved commodious enough to swallow four duffel bags, two dogs, and a week of groceries.

Example

When the scouts pitched the surplus army tent, they found it commodious beyond their hopes: twelve sleeping bags fit in a ring, packs stacked along the canvas, and there was still headroom to stand and dress by lantern light.

Commodious is more precise than just 'big' or 'roomy' because it praises space that serves comfort—room arranged so that living in it feels easy, not merely a large number of square feet.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

spacious: Spacious praises a place for offering plenty of open, usable room — a spacious lobby lets a crowd move freely. Commodious adds that the space is arranged so living and working in it feel easy. Both compliment space that serves people; neither describes hugeness that has outrun all use.

capacious: Capacious means able to hold a great deal — a capacious trunk swallows whatever you load into it, and the word measures pure holding power. Commodious cares about comfort instead: a commodious cabin offers generous, well-arranged room to live in, not just storage to fill.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

cramped: so short of space that moving is a struggle

poky: small, confined, and a little dismal

Where it sits · how far the space outruns the need — roomy → commodious → cavernous

roomy vs. commodious: Roomy stops short of commodious — a roomy trunk merely fits everything, while a commodious cabin offers generous space to live in.

cavernous vs. commodious: Cavernous goes further than commodious — a cavernous hangar is so vast it echoes, long past feeling comfortable.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — com-

Prefix — com-: with, together

Root — mod-

Root — mod-: measure (Latin modus)

Suffix — -ious

Suffix — -ious: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Com- (with) + mod- (measure) + -ious (full of) = having full measure. Latin commodus meant 'of proper measure, convenient,' and English stretched that convenience into physical room: a commodious space has measure to spare — enough room for everything, with comfort left over.

Use the root in a new word: accommodate

Use the root in a new word: accommodate: The renovated hostel can accommodate forty hikers on even the busiest weekend.

Word Building

Word Choice

formal / slightly old-fashioned

Commodious is a formal, slightly old-fashioned word that flatters a space: it says the room is not just large but comfortable to live and move in. For everyday talk, 'roomy' or 'spacious' is plainer; reach for commodious in a description meant to charm — a listing, a review, a tour.
